checks.name: Latin and Vietnamese legacy token normalization is preserved
vi: native-script lexical retrieval finds the authored source
en: native-script lexical retrieval finds the authored source
zh-CN: native-script lexical retrieval finds the authored source
ja: native-script lexical retrieval finds the authored source
ko: native-script lexical retrieval finds the authored source
Mixed Latin/CJK runs split without losing either script
Korean composed and decomposed syllables normalize identically
Japanese kana voicing is preserved rather than accent-stripped
Supplementary Han characters remain whole code points
Multi-character queries use adjacent bigrams, not isolated common characters
A deliberate one-character query remains searchable in a document
No bigram crosses a punctuation, whitespace or Latin-script boundary
Query terms are unique and bounded to forty
Input, token and token-length bounds prevent unbounded lexical allocation
Stop words, empty text, punctuation and emoji do not fabricate hits
Missing evidence in each authored language remains empty
Numeric conflict warning still works in Latin and East Asian text
Isolated SQLite CJK retrieval preserves exact source offsets and actor scope
Offline test makes no network/provider request

scope: Deterministic tokenizer/ranking with authored fixtures and one isolated in-memory SQLite provenance/ACL flow. Not semantic retrieval, real provider, OAuth, student trial or public-deployment validation.
limitations: Bigrams are lexical overlap, not word segmentation, translation or calibrated relevance.
Single-character searches can have low precision; no guarantee of semantic coverage.
Input/query/token caps are intentional lexical resource bounds; original source/citation text is unchanged.
